text.p: The main stories in the Austrian press this Wednesday are:
DER STANDARD
- Styrian People's Party official Gerhard Hirschmann wants to replace Austrian provincial parliaments with three new regions of east, west and south.
- Vienna has failed to put itself on the technology map, says Peter Mayerhofer of the Economic Research Institute Wifo. More firms are opting for Burgenland rather than the capital.
- Fewer people in Austria are dying, despite an increased population, according to the central statistical office (Statistischen Zentralamtes).
DIE PRESSE

- Both coalition parties, the Social Democrats and the conservative People's Party, are expected to back President Thomas Klestil when he stands for re-election, probably in September, although no official statement has been made.
- National Bank President Klaus Liebscher says he is 99 percent sure that EMU will be realised on time.
- Encouraged by good half-year results, Bawag General Director Helmuyt Elsner says his war chest is full enough to buy postal savings bank PSK.
- A study by the Austrian Hotel and Tourism Trust Company says that reorganisation could provide Austria's hotels with a way out of their crisis.
- Buoyant demand for Austrian goods, thanks to the strong dollar, will allow the export sector more investment, says an expert of the Economic Research Institute Wifo.
- Austrian Federal Railways have ordered 75 high-performance locomotives from Siemens. The engines will be delivered by 2002, with an option to buy a further 325.
KURIER
- Foreign workers will have to learn German in future.
- Energy market liberalisation: government wants to protect the Austrian electricity market from foreign involvement.
- Dollar strength sends energy prices higher. Danger of a rise in energy prices ahead of liberalisation, which government wants to prevent.
- Tolls for heavy goods vehicles will come into force by 1999, costing 1.50 schillings per km for vehicles weighing up to 12 tonnes and two schillings per km for heavier vehicles.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Bad news for the tourism industry: the number of overnight stays for the summer half year 1997 is, at 61 037 million, at its worst for a quarter of a century.
- Bad weather for the third summer running is a catastrophe for Austria's ice-cream business.
- Klaus Liebscher says he is basically happy with the government's 1998-1999 double budget.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT

- If hard currencies like the deutschmark and schilling are converted into euros while they are weak, it could lead to a loss of wealth, which it will be difficult to recover in the context of European economic and monetary union.
